summary: PulseGuard v0.6.41 fixes a v0.6.40 crash at the end of Fix & Optimize, treats the Windows 24-hour restore point limit as expected instead of a warning, and cleans up several result messages. It keeps all v0.6.40 safety changes.

sections.heading: Fix & Optimize finishes again
sections.detail: v0.6.40 crashed while writing the final summary because the Game Ready step no longer returns CPU before/after values. The post-fix rescan and final report now run normally.

sections.heading: Clearer results
sections.detail: A restore point made earlier the same day is reported as SKIPPED (Windows allows one per 24 hours) instead of a warning, the restore-point message no longer repeats itself, Deep Clean only records a change when it actually deleted files, and suppressed WinGet packages now say why in the update window.

sections.heading: Elevated helpers moved to a protected folder
sections.detail: Scripts, specs and installers that PulseGuard runs as administrator now live in C:\ProgramData\PulseGuard PC Elevated, which only Administrators and SYSTEM can change. The Software Protection SYSTEM-task fallback and its Windows permission edits were removed. Apps closed by Game Ready are relaunched unelevated. Daily scheduled scans are refused (and removed) while PulseGuard is installed in a folder standard programs can modify.

sections.heading: Updates ask first and can be signed
sections.detail: The updater now asks before installing, stages downloads in the protected folder, and verifies an RSA release signature once a public key is pinned in PulseGuard_Updater.ps1.

sections.heading: Fix & Optimize no longer removes your data
sections.detail: Registry cleaning is review-only, the Privacy Sweep is manual and keeps Quick Access pins and Jump Lists, PATH is never edited automatically, Deep Clean keeps browser/thumbnail caches and resumable downloads, and background-app closing is manual with Spotify, Teams, Creative Cloud and Epic removed from the close list.

sections.heading: Startup changes and Restore fixed
sections.detail: Run-key startup items are disabled with Task Manager's StartupApproved flag so they can be re-enabled from Task Manager. Restore now steps back one run at a time and restores registry values with their original type.

sections.heading: Truthful results
sections.detail: Restore points are verified before being reported as created, the WinGet helper defines every function it uses and fails safe on its retry-hold file, report lists stay JSON arrays, serial numbers are redacted from the report, and two calls to functions that did not exist were fixed.

sections.heading: Stability-aware advice
sections.detail: Several different BSOD codes now point to RAM/EXPO/CPU tuning first, memory running below its rated speed is treated as a possible stability test while crashes are active, and a BSOD is no longer counted twice through its Kernel-Power reboot.
